summary: Renames the client auth-strategy config field from `config.strategy` to `config.authStrategy` on both the Node entry (`Encryption()`) and the WASM entry (`@cipherstash/stack/wasm-inline`), keeping `strategy` as a deprecated alias that still forwards and emits a one-time console.warn; `authStrategy` wins when both are set. Most of the diff is TypeDoc. The public `Encryption()` path is backwards compatible and covered by updated unit tests for forwarding, alias, precedence and the WASM accessKey mutual-exclusion guard; CI test jobs (Node 22/24, Bun, E2E, WASM Deno E2E) report success. The one compatibility edge not covered by the alias is the `@internal` but runtime-public `EncryptionClient.init()` method, whose parameter was renamed without an alias: a direct caller still passing `strategy` would silently fall back to the default `auto` strategy. No in-repo caller does this. The FFI option name and payload format are unchanged, so there is no data-at-rest or wire-format effect. Advisory: focused review of the init() rename; otherwise low risk.

behaviour_changes.description: `ClientConfig` gains `authStrategy?: AuthStrategy`; `strategy` stays as a @deprecated alias. `Encryption()` resolves `authStrategy ?? strategy` and passes the result to `client.init` as `authStrategy`, which is forwarded to protect-ffi `newClient` under the unchanged FFI option name `strategy`.

`EncryptionClient.init()` config parameter renamed `strategy` → `authStrategy` with no alias. The method is tagged `@internal` but the class is exported via the `./encryption` subpath, so a direct caller passing `strategy` now has it ignored and protect-ffi builds its default auto strategy.
Passing the deprecated `strategy` field (Node or WASM entry) now logs a once-per-process `console.warn` deprecation message, including when `authStrategy` is also set.

WASM `WasmClientConfig` union gains an `authStrategy` arm (with optional deprecated `strategy`) and keeps a `strategy`-only arm; `resolveStrategy` resolves `authStrategy ?? strategy` and the accessKey mutual-exclusion guard now covers both fields, naming the field the caller set.

New exported test hook `__resetStrategyDeprecationWarningForTests` on both `@cipherstash/stack/encryption` and `@cipherstash/stack/wasm-inline` (marked @internal). Adds surface only; it resets the warning latch.

Large TypeDoc rewrite of `Encryption()` (auth strategies, env vars, lock context, keysets) and doc references updated from `config.strategy` to `config.authStrategy`. Root AGENTS.md still says `config.strategy`, which still works.

failure_scenarios.title: Direct EncryptionClient.init({ strategy }) caller silently loses its auth strategy
failure_scenarios.trigger: A consumer (plain JS, or TS passing a non-literal/spread object) constructs `new EncryptionClient()` from `@cipherstash/stack/encryption` and calls `init({ ..., strategy })`, as worked at base.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: At base `init` forwarded `config.strategy` to newClient (base encryption/index.ts:130,166). At head `init` reads only `config.authStrategy` (head :166 forwards `config.authStrategy`); the deprecated alias is resolved only inside `Encryption()` (head :864-881). An unrecognised `strategy` key is dropped, so `strategy: undefined` reaches protect-ffi and it builds the default auto strategy from CS_* env vars or the local dev profile.
failure_scenarios.consequence: If ambient credentials exist, ZeroKMS requests authenticate as the service/dev principal rather than the intended per-user OidcFederationStrategy identity; no warning is emitted. With lock context the operation would likely fail loudly; without it the user-identity binding of requests is lost silently. If no ambient credentials exist, init fails loudly. No ciphertext format or key change.
